sentence_stem: The new bridge was closed for repairs after
correct_completion: a serious crack had been found in one of its supports.
full_sentence: The new bridge was closed for repairs after a serious crack had been found in one of its supports.
acceptable_variants: engineers had discovered a serious crack in one of its supports.
inspectors had noticed damage to one of its supports.

options.text: the cars were driving across it every day.
options.why_wrong: This describes what happened before the closure, but it does not explain why the bridge was closed.

options.text: so the city will paint it next summer.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a result, but the sentence needs a past event that happened before the closure, not a future plan.

options.text: a serious crack had been found in one of its supports.
it was open to traffic again on Monday.
options.why_wrong: This describes what happened after the repairs, not the event that led to the closure.

grammar_focus: Passive voice with the past perfect after 'after'
explanation: After 'after', English needs a past perfect clause to show that the discovery happened first. The passive form had been found shows the crack was discovered before the closure. Spanish speakers sometimes use a simple past here, but English requires the past perfect to show the sequence of events.
translation: El nuevo puente fue cerrado para reparaciones después de que se encontrara una grieta grave en uno de sus soportes.
